title: The Quality Serenaders' history from a British magazine article
summary: Collette reads an article on the Quality Four's origins, the Victor sides and Lionel Hampton, which Howard confirms.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And what about the period when you started recording, is that too far away to tell about?
Yeah, too far away.
Could you fill us in on something before that? (inaudible) Because I see where you recorded with Victor.
I don't remember what I did with Victor but when I started with them --
Ms. Wilhard: (unintelligible) 1938 (unintelligible)

Paul Howard's Quality Serenaders with the great Los Angeles band, that recorded some 11 sides for Victor about 1930. Howard, now the popular secretary of the Los Angeles Colored Local 767 AFof M says that the group was really a cooperative affair and used his name because he was manager. The group originated in 1923 as the Quality Four, for a job at the Red Onion Cafe on Central Avenue. It included Leon Halpert (phonetic) Herriford.
That's right, Leon Halpert Herriford.
And Howard on saxes. Howie Brooks on piano and Henry Tin Pan Allen on drums.
That's right.
Howie Brooks Quality Four, the following sides were made for the Hollywood label, "Mistreatin'" and "Daddy" Frankie and goes on to --
Frankie and Daddy --
(Inaudible) out that's And it's all right, and it's over here. "Daddy" and "Frankie and Johnny."
Yeah, "Frankie and Johnny".
(Unintelligible) and Nobody's Sweetheart, "Who Will Get It" and "Down on the Farm".
"Down on the Farm", now we used to sing that, all of us.
Let's see, Brooks had just come to town with Mamie Smith's Jazz Hounds. That sound familiar?
Oh, yeah.

January 1938 that was (inaudible) and a "Tempo" magazine decided to stay. The Four was very successful and soon begin to add men. Thomas Valentine on banjo and George Youngdahl, now Orendorff with Les Hite and Al Westlight on trumpets, were the first in 1925 for a job at Lyman's Alabam.
What Lyman is that? Is that --
Mack Lyman.

They added Lewis Taylor now with Earl Hines, on trombone and none other than Lionel Hampton on drums. Lionel had been brought out from Milwaukee by Reb Spikes and had settled in Los Angeles. He was playing an awful lot then, though he had not yet taken up the vibes. He did play his two-finger piano which he originated contrary to other reports.
Nothing you can add to it.
It's pretty clear then.
I was adding to the band all the time, trying to make it better.
